newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia using bank credits to net tax, company debt.
newsitem.headline: Russia using bank credits to net tax, company debt.

text.p: The Russian Finance Ministry has begun a programme using commercial bank credits to net out tax and commercial debts between companies and the government, an official said on Tuesday.

Anton Siluanov, head of the ministry's department of macroeconomics and monetary credit policy, told Reuters that the plan had been signed into action by Finance Minister Alexander Livshits on September 17 and would last until year end.
Companies are no longer allowed to net out debts with each other directly.
"This cancelling out of debts will exist until the end of the year, but only using commercial bank credits... direct netting out as of July 1 no longer exists," he said.
The Russian economy has been almost paralysed by a web of interlocking mutual debts and unpaid bills.
Many companies are behind in settling each other's bills and in paying taxes, and the government in turn has not paid money it owes companies and is behind on many wage payments.
The federal government collected only about 74 percent of targetted taxes in the first nine months of the year.
According to the plan, firms which owe taxes can borrow from commercial banks and use the credits to pay taxes.
The government, which receives the credits as tax payment, uses the credits to pay off its own debts to firms, which can then pay back the credits to the banks.
"Firms which are debtors to the budget send such credits to the budget, which then returns them to those owed by the budget and then to the banks," Siluanov said.
He did not name banks which could offer the credits and did not say to what extent credits were being used.
